name: Affenpinscher

Large, round, dark eyes and a pushed-in nose are breed hallmarks. Ears are small and either cropped (in countries where permitted) or natural and folded. name: Airedale Terrier
appearance: Airedales are the largest terrier breed — males typically 50–65 lbs, females 40–55 lbs, standing approximately 23 inches at the shoulder. The build is athletic and substantial: a strong, level topline, well-muscled quarters, and a confident, upright carriage that broadcasts their self-assurance. name: American Eskimo Dog
appearance: The American Eskimo Dog is a Nordic-type Spitz, with all the hallmarks of that group: a wedge-shaped head, erect triangular ears, a thick double coat, and a tail curled over the back. The body is well-proportioned — neither heavy-boned nor fine-boned — with a deep chest, level topline, and strong, well-muscled hindquarters that give the breed its agile, efficient movement. name: Australian Terrier
appearance: The Australian Terrier is a sturdy, low-set, moderately long dog with a characteristic outline that's immediately recognizable. The body is longer than it is tall, giving it a rectangular profile different from the more square-bodied terriers. The chest is deep and the legs are short but straight and strong. name: Bearded Collie
appearance: The Bearded Collie is a medium-sized, athletic dog with a sturdy build that belies its agility. Males typically stand 21–22 inches at the shoulder, while females measure 20–21 inches. Weight ranges from 45 to 55 pounds, with most dogs landing solidly in the middle of that range. The breed's most defining feature is its magnificent double coat. name: Beauceron
appearance: The Beauceron is a large, well-muscled dog that projects strength and elegance simultaneously. Males stand 25.5–27.5 inches at the shoulder and females 24–26.5 inches. Weight ranges from 70 to 110 pounds, with most males weighing 85–100 pounds. The body is slightly longer than tall, with a strong, level back and a deep chest. name: Bedlington Terrier
appearance: The Bedlington is small but not fragile — males and females typically weigh 17–23 lbs and stand 15–17.5 inches at the shoulder. The narrow, pear-shaped head, deep-set almond eyes, and the distinctive topknot of lighter, fluffy hair create the breed's lamb-like silhouette. name: Belgian Sheepdog
appearance: The Belgian Sheepdog is a medium-to-large dog with a graceful, well-proportioned build. Males typically stand 24–26 inches at the shoulder and weigh 55–75 pounds; females are slightly smaller at 22–24 inches and 45–60 pounds. name: Belgian Tervuren
appearance: The Belgian Tervuren is a medium-to-large, well-proportioned dog with a square, athletic build. Males typically stand 24–26 inches at the shoulder and weigh 55–75 pounds; females stand 22–24 inches and weigh 45–60 pounds. name: Border Terrier
appearance: Small and workmanlike — 11–16 lbs, 11–16 inches tall, built for function rather than show ring glamour. The head is distinctive: otter-like, with a broad skull, short muzzle, and dark, keen eyes. The body is compact and narrow through the chest — designed to fit through underground passages. name: Bouvier des Flandres
appearance: The Bouvier des Flandres is a large, powerfully built dog with a compact, square body that conveys strength and agility. Males stand 24.5–27.5 inches at the shoulder and weigh 70–110 pounds; females are slightly smaller at 23.5–26.5 inches. name: Briard
appearance: The Briard is a large, muscular, well-proportioned dog with a powerful build that conveys both strength and agility. Males stand 23–27 inches at the shoulder and weigh 70–100 pounds; females are slightly smaller at 22–25.5 inches and 55–75 pounds. name: Brussels Griffon
appearance: The Brussels Griffon is a compact, sturdy little dog with a notably large, domed head relative to its body size. The face is the breed's defining feature: the pushed-in muzzle (brachycephalic), large, prominent dark eyes, and prominent chin create the famous monkey or human-like expression. name: Cairn Terrier
appearance: The Cairn Terrier's appearance beautifully reflects its working heritage: this is a compact, sturdy dog built to move through rough terrain and dig with determination. The overall impression should be that of a small, active terrier — broader in proportion to its length than many other small breeds, with a distinctive wide head and short strong muzzle. name: Chinese Crested
appearance: The Hairless variety has smooth, soft, warm skin — often described as feeling like human skin — that may be solid in color or spotted. The skin tone varies considerably from pink to dark gray to black, with many dogs having a mottled combination. name: Chinese Shar-Pei
appearance: The Chinese Shar-Pei's appearance is unique in the dog world. The head is large and somewhat disproportionate to the body, covered in excess loose skin that creates deep folds over the forehead and face. name: Coton de Tulear
appearance: The Coton de Tulear is a small, well-balanced dog with a slightly longer body than it is tall. The coat is the dominant physical feature: long, thick, and profuse over the entire body, with a texture that is soft and cottony rather than silky or wiry. name: Entlebucher Mountain Dog
appearance: The Entlebucher Mountain Dog is a compact, sturdy, and well-muscled dog. The coat is short and tight, with the classic Swiss Sennenhund tricolor pattern: a black base coat with symmetrical rust and white markings. name: Finnish Lapphund
appearance: The Finnish Lapphund is a medium-sized, well-balanced dog with a substantial double coat that makes it appear larger than its actual weight. The outer coat is long, straight to slightly wavy, and coarse; the undercoat is dense, soft, and provides exceptional insulation. name: Finnish Spitz
appearance: The Finnish Spitz is a square, medium-sized dog with clean lines and a lively, spirited bearing. The head is fox-like with a moderately narrow muzzle, almond-shaped dark eyes, and sharply erect ears that are high-set and always active. The expression is keen and intelligent. name: Giant Schnauzer
appearance: Large and powerfully built with a rectangular silhouette — the body length roughly equals the height at the withers. Males stand 25.5–27.5 inches at the shoulder; females 23.5–25.5 inches. Weight ranges from 55–85 lbs, with males at the heavier end. name: Greater Swiss Mountain Dog
appearance: Large and powerfully built — this is a breed that looks like it was designed to pull a loaded cart, because it was. Males stand 25.5–28.5 inches at the shoulder and typically weigh 105–140 lbs; females 23.5–27 inches and 85–110 lbs. The build is muscular and substantial without being bulky or slow-looking. name: Icelandic Sheepdog
appearance: The Icelandic Sheepdog is a compact, well-proportioned spitz-type dog. The head is strongly made with a moderately broad skull, a clearly defined stop, and a muzzle that is slightly shorter than the skull length. Ears are erect, medium-sized, and triangular. name: Irish Terrier
appearance: Medium-sized and racily built — males and females both fall in the 25–27 lb range and stand around 18 inches at the shoulder. The Irish Terrier has a long, flat head with small V-shaped ears that fold forward, dark, alert eyes, and the upright tail that typifies terrier breeds. name: Japanese Chin
appearance: The Japanese Chin's most arresting feature is its face: a very flat profile, a broad skull, wide-set large dark eyes, and a nose set high between the eyes — a configuration that gives the breed its characteristic surprised, open expression. name: Keeshond
appearance: Medium-sized and compact — 35 to 45 pounds, 17 to 18 inches at the shoulder. The profuse double coat creates a lion's mane effect around the neck and chest (the ruff), with thick fur on the hindquarters forming distinctive "trousers." name: Kerry Blue Terrier
appearance: The Kerry Blue Terrier's most immediately striking feature is its wavy, dense coat in blue-gray shades — a color that exists in very few dog breeds. The coat should be soft and wavy (not curly or straight), dense, and of medium length. name: Komondor
appearance: Large and powerful — males are typically 100+ lbs and over 27 inches at the shoulder, making the Komondor one of the largest breeds by mass. The build is muscular and substantial beneath the coat. The head is broad, the expression calm and serious. name: Lakeland Terrier
appearance: The Lakeland Terrier is a small, well-balanced dog that conveys strength and agility despite its modest size. The head is rectangular and flat-skulled, with a strong, well-filled muzzle approximately equal in length to the skull. name: Leonberger
appearance: Massive, lion-like, and striking. Males are considerably larger than females — males typically weigh 130–170 lbs and stand 28–31.5 inches; females 90–130 lbs and 25.5–29.5 inches. The overall impression is of a powerful but elegant giant — not the shapeless bulk of some mastiff breeds, but a well-proportioned, muscular dog with clear working-dog structure. name: Lhasa Apso
appearance: Small and sturdy — 12 to 18 pounds, 10 to 11 inches at the shoulder. The body is slightly longer than tall, and the whole structure is solid beneath all that coat. The heavy fall of hair over the face is protective in origin — it shielded the dog's eyes from the harsh Himalayan wind and sun. name: Lowchen
appearance: The Lowchen has a moderate, well-balanced build — sturdy for its size, with a level topline, good bone, and a head that is broad and relatively short-muzzled with a warm, expressive face. The large, round, dark eyes and the gently wavy coat give the dog a soft, appealing expression that is simultaneously charming and alert. The coat is the breed's most visually distinctive feature. name: Miniature Bull Terrier
appearance: The Miniature Bull Terrier's most recognizable feature is its head — long, strong, and egg-shaped when viewed from the front, with no stop and a surface that arcs gently from the top of the skull down to the tip of the nose. name: Miniature Pinscher
appearance: The Miniature Pinscher is a well-balanced, compact dog with a sturdy, muscular build. His body is square in proportion, with a level topline and a deep chest that gives him an air of substance despite his small frame. name: Norfolk Terrier
appearance: The Norfolk Terrier has a compact, low, well-boned body. It is slightly longer than it is tall, with a level topline and strong hindquarters. The head is broad and slightly rounded, with dark oval eyes that convey boldness and intelligence. The defining feature is its V-shaped drop ears, which fold forward and lie close to the skull — always in motion when the dog is alert. The coat is hard, wiry,

name: Norwich Terrier
appearance: The Norwich Terrier is a compact, low, sturdy dog. The body is short and level, with good substance for its size — heavy bone and strong musculature belie the small frame. The head is slightly rounded, the muzzle wedge-shaped and strong. The prick ears are small, erect, and set wide apart on a broad skull, giving the breed its characteristic open, alert expression. name: Otterhound
appearance: Large and heavily built, males typically 115 lbs, females somewhat lighter. name: Papillon
appearance: The Papillon is a fine-boned, dainty dog with a light, elegant build that somehow manages to look both fragile and athletic. The body is slightly longer than it is tall, with a well-rounded ribcage, level topline, and a long, plumed tail carried arched over the back. name: Parson Russell Terrier
appearance: The Parson Russell Terrier is a well-balanced, athletic dog whose appearance reflects its working heritage. The breed standard calls for a body that is slightly longer than tall, with a small, flexible chest that allows the dog to squeeze through underground burrows — a practical feature of its fox-hunting origins. name: Pekingese
appearance: The Pekingese is built close to the ground with a heavy front end, wide chest, and somewhat bowed forelegs that give him his characteristic rolling, unhurried gait. The body is pear-shaped — heavier in the front than the rear — and surprisingly solid and substantial despite a small overall frame. The topline is level and the hindquarters are lighter than the front. The head is large relative to th

name: Polish Lowland Sheepdog
appearance: The Polish Lowland Sheepdog's most immediately recognizable feature is its profuse, shaggy double coat, which covers the entire body including the face and eyes. The outer coat is long, dense, and of harsh or crisp texture; the undercoat is soft and dense. The coat does not have a natural wave or curl but hangs flat in a shaggy curtain. name: Puli

The cords hang from all parts of the body — head, body, legs, and tail — in long, flat-to-round rope-like locks that completely obscure the dog's underlying structure. name: Redbone Coonhound

The coat is the breed's most distinctive feature: short, dense, and a rich, deep red — one of the most uniformly solid-colored of the hound breeds. name: Russell Terrier

name: Schipperke
appearance: The Schipperke's silhouette is distinctive and immediately recognizable. The body is slightly longer than tall, with a level topline that slopes slightly toward the naturally raised rear — a slope emphasized by the longer coat over the withers and shoulders compared to the rear. name: Scottish Deerhound
appearance: Large and rangy — males 85–110 lbs, standing 30–32 inches; females 75–95 lbs, somewhat smaller. The rough, wiry coat in shades of blue-grey, brindle, or grey gives the Deerhound a slightly shaggy, aristocratic appearance. name: Scottish Terrier
appearance: The Scottish Terrier's appearance is immediately recognizable: a long, low body set on short but powerful legs, a large rectangular head with prominent beard and eyebrows, upright pointed ears, and an upright tail carried erect or with a slight forward curl. The breed's proportions — relatively long body for its height, with a large, heavily furnished head — give it an unusual and distinctive appe

name: Silky Terrier
appearance: The Silky Terrier is a moderately low-set dog with a refined, compact build. The body is slightly longer than it is tall, giving it an alert, forward-leaning stance. Its wedge-shaped head is carried high, with dark almond-shaped eyes that sparkle with intelligence and mischief. The ears are small, V-shaped, and erect — always pricked, always listening. name: Skye Terrier
appearance: The Skye Terrier is built quite differently from most terriers — it is remarkably long in proportion to its height, with a body roughly twice as long as it is tall. This low, powerful silhouette was purpose-built for working in underground dens. name: Spanish Water Dog
appearance: Medium-sized and solidly built — males typically 40–49 lbs and 17.75–19.75 inches at the shoulder; females 31–40 lbs and 15.75–18 inches. The body is slightly longer than tall, with the muscular, athletic build of a dog designed to work all day across varied terrain. The face is broad, with almond-shaped eyes in hazel to chestnut brown and pendant ears that hang flat against the head. The coat is

name: Standard Schnauzer
appearance: Compact, squarely built, and muscular. The body length equals the height at the withers, giving the classic rectangular-blocked Schnauzer silhouette. Males stand 18.5–19.5 inches; females 17.5–18.5 inches. Weight runs 30–45 lbs for females, 35–50 lbs for males. The build is athletic and capable without being heavy. The wiry double coat is the breed's signature. The outer coat is hard and wiry; the

name: Swedish Vallhund
appearance: The Swedish Vallhund's body is longer than it is tall — a build shared by other herding breeds that worked cattle by nipping at heels and staying low to avoid kicks. The legs are short but strongly muscled; the chest is long and well-developed; the back is level and strong. The overall impression is of a compact, powerful, purpose-built working dog. name: Tibetan Spaniel
appearance: The Tibetan Spaniel has a small, slightly domed head — a characteristic shared with several other Tibetan breeds — with a medium-length, blunt muzzle, a slight undershot or level bite, and large, dark, slightly wide-set eyes that give the face its warm, watchful expression. The ears are pendant and feathered, hanging close to the head. The overall expression combines intelligence, warmth, and rese

name: Tibetan Terrier
appearance: Medium-sized and squarely built, weighing 18–30 lbs and standing 14–17 inches at the shoulder. The hallmark feature is the long, flowing double coat — a soft woolly undercoat beneath a fine, straight-to-wavy outer coat that can be any color or combination. name: Toy Fox Terrier
appearance: The Toy Fox Terrier has a balanced, athletic build — compact but never coarse. The body is square in proportion, with a level back and a well-muscled rear. The head is slightly rounded, the muzzle tapered, and the expression is keen and alert. The large, erect ears frame the face and give the breed its characteristic look of constant attention. The smooth, short coat lies flat against the body and

name: Welsh Terrier
appearance: The Welsh Terrier has a square, well-proportioned build — the body length approximately equal to the height at the shoulder. The head is long and flat, the muzzle strong, and the expression is alert and intelligent. The small, V-shaped ears fold forward and lie close to the skull. The eyes are small, dark, and full of fire. The coat is hard, wiry, and dense — the outer coat protecting a softer und

name: Wire Fox Terrier
appearance: The Wire Fox Terrier's build is a study in proportion and power. The back is short and level; the chest is deep rather than wide; the legs are straight and well-boned. The neck is long and muscular, flowing cleanly into well-laid-back shoulders. The overall silhouette — square, balanced, and upstanding — is one of the most recognizable in the dog world. The wiry coat is the breed's signature featu

name: Xoloitzcuintli
appearance: Toy Xolos weigh 10–15 lbs; Miniatures 15–30 lbs; Standards 30–55 lbs. All three sizes share the same lean, elegant build — almond-shaped eyes, large bat-like ears, a smooth or hairless body, and a sleek, athletic silhouette. The Xolo is built like a primitive dog: functional, without exaggeration in any direction. The hairless variety's skin can range from dark gray-black to bronze, spotted, or pa

name: Goldendoodle
appearance: Size varies enormously by Poodle parent. Mini Goldendoodles (Mini Poodle parent) typically weigh 15-35 lbs and stand 14-17 inches at the shoulder. Standard Goldendoodles (Standard Poodle parent) typically weigh 50-90 lbs and stand 20-24 inches. Coat type is the most variable feature: straight (more Golden Retriever), wavy (intermediate), or curly (more Poodle). F1B and multigen dogs are more reliably wavy or curly. Colors include cream, apricot, red, chocolate, black, and parti (multiple colors). The teddy-bear face and expressive dark eyes are characteristic.

name: Labradoodle
appearance: Size depends on the Poodle parent. Miniature Labradoodles (Mini Poodle parent) typically weigh 15-25 lbs. Standard Labradoodles (Standard Poodle parent) typically weigh 50-85 lbs and stand 21-24 inches. Coat types are categorized as hair (Labrador-type, sheds), fleece (soft and wavy, low-shedding), or wool (curly and dense, minimal-shedding). Australian Labradoodle breeders work specifically toward fleece and wool coats. Colors include cream, gold, apricot, red, chocolate, black, parchment, lavender, and parti combinations.

name: Bernedoodle
appearance: Standard Bernedoodles stand 23-29 inches and weigh 50-90 lbs. Mini Bernedoodles stand 18-22 inches and weigh 25-49 lbs. Tiny/Toy Bernedoodles weigh 10-24 lbs. Coat is wavy or curly and ranges from low-shedding to minimally-shedding. The signature tri-color pattern - black with white markings and rust accents over the eyes and on the cheeks and legs - mirrors the Bernese Mountain Dog. Other patterns include bi-color (black and white), sable, merle, and solid colors. Substantial, sturdy build.

name: Cavapoo
appearance: Small, compact, and rounded. Adult Cavapoos typically weigh 9-25 lbs and stand 9-14 inches at the shoulder. The Toy Poodle parent produces smaller Cavapoos; the Miniature Poodle parent produces the upper end of the range. Coats are wavy or curly, with F1B and multigen Cavapoos leaning curlier. Colors include cream, apricot, red, chocolate, black, sable, tri-color (Blenheim-pattern from the Cavalier side), and parti combinations. Dark eyes and rounded teddy-bear muzzle give the breed its distinctive look.

name: Sheepadoodle
appearance: Standard Sheepadoodles stand 18-24 inches and weigh 55-85 lbs. Mini Sheepadoodles stand 15-20 inches and weigh 30-55 lbs. The build is square, well-boned, and athletic. Coat is typically wavy or curly. The signature panda coloring - black with white markings on the chest, face, paws, and tail tip - is the most common and most sought-after pattern. Solid black, solid white, blue merle, and tri-color also occur. The coat is dense and grows continuously like the Poodle's; coat density is higher than other Doodles.

name: Aussiedoodle
appearance: Standard Aussiedoodles stand 18-23 inches and weigh 45-70 lbs. Mini Aussiedoodles stand 14-17 inches and weigh 25-45 lbs. Build is square, athletic, and built for sustained activity. Coat is wavy or curly. The signature feature is the merle pattern - a mottled, marbled coat in blue merle (gray-blue with black patches), red merle (copper with brown patches), or rare phantom merle. White markings on the chest, face, paws, and tail tip are common. Solid colors also occur: black, red, chocolate, sable. Eyes are often striking - blue, amber, or heterochromia (one of each color).
